title: Unify soft/hard wrap handling to correct line break handling for ICU 79
description:
Upgrading from ICU 78.3 to ICU 79 broke {textshaping}'s tests; LLM offered this proposed fix with explanation:

---

Previously, `HarfBuzzShaper::add_string()` inserted all boundaries from `hard_wrap` (`stringi::stri_locate_all_boundaries(..., skip_line_soft = TRUE)`) directly into `hard_break`, assuming they always corresponded to explicit line-break characters. Under ICU 79, this caused the final character of every string to be treated as a paragraph-terminating line break, popped from the shaped glyphs, and followed by an out-of-bounds vector access in `HarfBuzzShaper::finish_string()`.

* Check `glyph_is_linebreak(full_string[break_pos])` when processing `hard_wrap` in `HarfBuzzShaper::add_string()` so non-linebreak end-of-text boundaries are recorded in `soft_break` instead of `hard_break`.
* Fix the off-by-one index in `HarfBuzzShaper::finish_string()` when accessing `ascenders` and `descenders` after a trailing hard break.

---

ICU 79 is currently just RC, see https://github.com/unicode-org/icu/releases/tag/release-79.1rc.

Yet-another-shaping-rewirte
description:
Fix #49 as well as a lot of quality-of-life improvements

This new engine version brings a number of features to the table. You can now specify the global direction of your text or let it be deduced from the text itself. If the global direction is rtl, then indent and hanging will be applied to the right side. Further, bidi text is correctly assembled for global rtl text (the core issue of #49).

`align` gains an `"auto"` and `"justified"` setting that will change between left and right based on the global direction of the text. The metrics slot in the return value of `shape_text()` will also report the global direction of the text.

The shaping engine now uses ICU (through stringi) to figure out valid soft and hard line break positions. This means that line wrapping for text runs including ideographic scripts are now more correct.

Lastly it adds a set of text generators and a plotting function that is useful for sanity checking the veracity of the shaping

title: Clarify conversion from r_bool
description:
In the upcoming release of cpp11 we introduce a r_bool type, however
this type can convert to and from both Rboolean and int, which produces
an ambiguity. Explicitly casting to int resolves it.
